M/S Ashoka Biryani vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 June, 2024 
Author: Parth Prateem Sahu
Bench: Parth Prateem Sahu
 1
 Nafr
 High Court Of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur
 Wpc No. 2629 of 2024 
1- M/s Ashoka Biryani, Through Its Partner Kalpana Tiwari D/o Shri Ram Chandra Tiwari, Aged About 43 Years, R/o G-1420,
Millennium Chowk, Sundar Nagar, Near Football House, P.S.-
D.D. Nagar, Raipur, Distt. - Raipur, C.G.
2- Kalpana Tiwari, Partner- M/s Ashoka Biryani D/o Shri Ram Chandra Tiwari, Aged About 45 Years, R/o G-1420, Millennium Chowk, Sundar Nagar, Near Football House, P.S.- D.D. Nagar,
Raipur, Distt. - Raipur, C.G.
3- Animesh Pandey, Partner -M/s Ashoka Biryani, S/o Shri Vibhuti Bhushan Pandey, Aged About 29 Years, R/o Agroha Colony, Near Raipura Chowk, P.S.- D.D. Nagar, Raipur, Distt. -
Raipur, C.G.
 ---- Petitioners  Versus 1- State Of Chhattisgarh, Through Collector, Raipur, Distt. -
Raipur, C.G.
2- Municipal Corporation Raipur, Through Commissioner,
Municipal Corporation Raipur, Distt. - Raipur, C.G.
3- Tahsildar, Tahsil And Distt. - Raipur, C.G.
 ---- Respondents For Petitioners : Mr. Kishore Bhaduri, Sr. Advocate with Mr. Ashutosh Pandey, Advocate & Mr.
Sabyasachi Bhaduri, Advocate For Respondents/State : Mr. Keshav Prasad Gupta, G.A. For Respondent No.2 : Mr. Pankaj Agrawal, Advocate Hon'ble Shri Justice Parth Prateem Sahu Order On Board 14/06/2024Sd/- Sd/-
1. With the consent of the parties, the matter is heard finally. 
M/S Ashoka Biryani vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44893583/
1 2. Petitioners have filed this petition alleging the action of sealing of shops run by petitioners in the name and style of M/s. Ashoka Biryani situated at Labhandi, Raipura Chowk, Pachpedi Naka,
Mahoba Bazar and Station Road Raipur by respondents on 19.04.2024 and 20.04.2024 to be without any authority of law. 
3. Learned counsel for petitioners contended that the documents, which is placed along with covering memo by State counsel, only shows that one panchnama was prepared mentioning that officials of the State Administration as also the officials of Police and the Municipal Corporation have conducted joint inspection in the business premises of petitioners and found that it was not having any fire safety measures as also not maintaining hygiene, there was no appropriate parking place available, however, petitioners were not served with any show cause notice by the specific department or the competent authority. If any order or action is to be taken for lapses or irregularities, if any, found in the business premises of petitioners then it is the appropriate authority who could have taken action against petitioners. From perusal of the panchnama or action, it is only appearing that shops were sealed under the order of Zone Commissioner, Municipal Corporation, Raipur who has no jurisdiction and authority of law to seal the business premises of petitioners for the lapses, if any, found as mentioned in the Panchanama. 
4. Learned State counsel submits that after getting the advance copy, he sought instructions and he was informed that joint inspection was done on 19.04.2024 and 20.04.2024. After inspection of business premises shortcomings and the irregularities were found. In panchnama it is mentioned that premises was not having fire safety measures, no appropriate parking place and premises was found to be unhygienic. However, when this Court posed query as to whether the officers who conducted panchanama informed the concerned department or officials, who could have taken any action under the safety measures or to the Food Department, he submits that authority who gave information has not given any instruction in this regard. No show cause notice was issued. 
5. Learned counsel for respondents- Municipal Corporation submits that the joint inspection was conducted and thereafter, three shops of petitioners were sealed under the order of Zone Commissioner, Zone - 9, Raipur and two shops have been sealed by State officials. However, when the question is posed to learned counsel for Municipal Corporation as to under what provision of law, the Zone Commissioner has taken such steps of sealing the shops/business premises of petitioners, he could not answer the query made by this Court. However, learned counsel lastly submits that if petitioners give an undertaking that they will run the business after complying all the provisions of law, they will open the shops of petitioners. 
6. Reply has been filed on behalf of respondent No.2- Municipal Corporation, in which there is no specific pleadings as to under which provisions of law, the action of sealing of shops has been taken. 
Learned State counsel submits that he is not intending to file reply as he has produced the copy of relevant documents, which is being relied upon.
7. At this stage, learned counsel for petitioners submits that petitioners are under an obligation to comply with the permission/license which was issued by the competent authority permitting petitioners for running their business, however, the action on the part of the respondents is per-se M/S Ashoka Biryani vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44893583/ 
2 arbitrary, illegal and therefore, this petition be allowed. He relied upon the decision of this Court in case of E.S. Beena & Anr. Vs. State of Chhattisgarh, through : Principal Secretary & Ors., reported in 2022 SCC OnLine Chh. 1454.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents placed on record. 
9. Perusal of the pleadings, documents placed on record as also considering the submission of learned counsel for respective parties, it is appearing that petitioners are running restaurant in the name and style of M/s. Ashoka Biryani at different locations within Raipur city. On 18.04.2024 two of the employees of petitioners while cleaning sewerage died, concerned police station was given morgue intimation and on 19.04.2024 and 20.04.2024, the restaurant run by petitioners at different locations were sealed. The main ground raised by learned counsel for petitioners is that the act of sealing of restaurants of petitioners by officials of Municipal Corporation and State administration is without jurisdiction and without authority of law. When the query is posed to learned counsel for respective respondents as to under which provisions of law, the restaurant run by petitioners were sealed, they only submitted that upon joint inspection they found that there is no proper fire safety measure, no proper parking place is available and kitchen and washroom were found unhygienic,
however, they could not able to point out as to under which provisions of law, the action is taken.
10. The State officials who are working under the State Government or of Municipal Corporation no doubt can take action but in accordance with law and under the specific statute or provisions of law,
only by the competent authority as prescribed therein.
11. In the panchnama which is placed on record by learned State counsel, prepared at the time of joint inspection would show that kitchen and washroom were in unhygienic conditions, however, it is not specifically mentioned in the panchnama that as to why the kitchen was found to be in unhygienic condition. There is no specific mention in this regard. With respect to no proper place of parking also or not having fire safety measures no show cause notice was issued to petitioners before sealing the premises by the competent authority providing opportunity of hearing. 
12. It is not a case of respondents that petitioners was running the business without having any prior permission or license for running the restaurant. Apart from the aforementioned two points, which was noted in the panchanama that kitchen and washroom were in unhygienic condition and no proper place of parking is available, the inspection team recorded that there was no fire safety measure for that also, show cause notice ought to have been issued by the competent authority and action, if any, for lapses of not establishing the fire safety measure within the premises can only be taken by the competent authority in accordance with law. 
13. For the forgoing discussions made here-in-above this Court is of the view that the action on the part of the respondents authorities of sealing the shops of petitioners is per-se arbitrary and illegal,
therefore, the respondents are directed to unseal the restaurant run by petitioners at Labhandi,
Raipura Chowk, Pachpedi Naka, Mahoba Bazar and Station Road Raipur by tomorrow. However,
the respondents are at liberty to take action against petitioners for violation of the conditions of license, any order or law, if any, after following due process of law and after giving show cause notice M/S Ashoka Biryani vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44893583/
3 and opportunity of hearing to petitioners. 
14. Accordingly, this petition is allowed. 
Sd/-
(Parth Prateem Sahu) Judge Balram M/S Ashoka Biryani vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44893583/
